decisions.reason: As a classic handle close to the core range, it is inexpensive to carry and still has option value while market acceptance settles in a growing construction-related market.
This handle family fits the established business and broad portfolio logic, so the firm would usually keep it unless overlap within the range quickly proves too high.
A new handle design near the existing offer is a low-commitment extension, and without clear negative evidence the firm is likely to preserve the option for another year.
Because it is another adjacent design innovation with limited additional carrying cost, management would likely wait for more demand information before withdrawing it.
Although portfolio crowding makes rationalization somewhat more plausible for this handle family, it still supports system breadth and is likely to be retained absent poor results.
As a flagship electronic access system aligned with the firm's strategic move toward digital building organization, it has high strategic option value and is unlikely to be dropped so soon.
